title_eng: Analysis of the effects of obesity and age on the risk of death from sepsis
title_kor: 패혈증 사망 위험에 미치는 비만도와 나이 영향 분석
abstract:
This study examines the obesity paradox in sepsis patients through an age-stratified survival analysis of 44,599 adults with 
an adult sepsis event. Cox proportional hazards models showed that underweight patients had consistently higher mortality risk 
(hazard ratio [HR] 1.3–2.1), while obesity was linked to lower mortality (HR 0.5 –0.7) only in the 35–64 and 75–84 age groups. 
The obesity paradox was not observed in younger or very elderly patients. The hazard ratio trends indicate that underweight 
patients experience a declining risk of mortality with advancing age, while obese patients exhibit elevated risk during middle 
age (35–64 years) followed by a reduced risk in older age, highlighting an age-dependent association between body mass index 
and sepsis outcomes.
